summary: Both sides now render (the old orig white-out is gone and the port is no longer black), and de-aliased at 160x160 they are recognizably the same kind of filamentary plasma — but the port's field runs at roughly 40x too fine a spatial scale and ~30x too fast in time, has no centre-weighted envelope, is ~2.4x too dim, and sits ~70 degrees too blue, so on the default 16x16 rig it reads as pastel pixel snow rather than a glowing coral blob.
observations: Re-judge context: the prior verdict's premise no longer holds. On this worktree (portSha256 810cf3f3ef42, epeSha256 6c2678ea26ac, harnessSha256 bfd91d43d7f9, identical across all 16 runs below) the ORIGINAL renders a normal, dark, structured field — baseline 6 s @ 20 fps on the default grid/16x16/256 px gives orig meanBrightness avg 46.1 (min 34, max 83), motion avg 2.6, zeroMotionFrames 1/120 — not the 255/255/255 white-out the old file described. The PORT also renders and animates: meanBrightness avg 18.9 (min 11, max 27), motion avg 23.4, motionLit 35.4, zeroMotionFrames 1/120. Neither side reports a compileError or runtimeError.

Control surface matches and is empty: meta.json sides.orig.controls and sides.port.controls are both [], and --probe-controls prints '(no settable controls)' for both sides. Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both), so the beat120 feed is irrelevant here.

ORIGINAL, structure (default 16x16 grid): a single large, smooth, organic blob occupying the centre of the grid — a white/pale core, a bright green rim, cyan/teal ridges fading into near-black navy voids at the edges. It morphs continuously (arms extend and retract, the core slides and rotates) with no discrete regimes or resets anywhere in a 240 s @ 2 fps survey.

PORT, structure (default 16x16 grid): dim, scattered single-pixel speckle in cyan/blue/violet on black. No blob, no core, no rim, no voids — the contact sheet at 0.0-6.0 s is indistinguishable from pastel TV snow, and the rhythm image is a flat uniform noise band with no column structure at all.

Spatial coherence, quantified (--dump, luminance neighbour correlation). Default 16x16 grid, t=0/0.05/0.1/0.5/3/3.05 s: orig h-corr 0.772-0.895 and v-corr 0.743-0.888 (a genuinely smooth field); port h-corr -0.049..0.183 and v-corr 0.046-0.099 (statistically indistinguishable from per-pixel noise at this resolution).

De-aliased at 160x160 the port turns out NOT to be hash noise — it is the same family of field at a far finer scale. Correlation-vs-lag along a row at t=0: orig 1px 0.998, 2px 0.993, 4px 0.975, 8px 0.920, 16px 0.806, 32px 0.711, 64px 0.691, 80px 0.615 (half-correlation lag never reached inside 80 px, i.e. > 50% of the canvas). Port: 1px 0.738, 2px 0.493, 4px 0.275, 8px 0.172, 16px 0.055, and flat noise beyond (half-correlation lag 2.0 px = 1.25% of the canvas). The port's feature scale is therefore at least ~40x too small.

The 160x160 renders make it visual: orig.png is one huge white-cored, green-rimmed blob filling the frame with soft dark lobes around it; port.png is a dense fine mesh of 2-4 px cyan/violet filaments covering the whole frame — the same ridged plasma morphology, shrunk by roughly one and a half orders of magnitude and dimmed.

Temporal coherence, quantified. Original (20 fps dumps of one run): whole-frame correlation with t=0 is 0.980 at 0.05 s, 0.936 at 0.10 s, 0.794 at 0.25 s, 0.644 at 0.5 s, 0.349 at 1 s — a half-decorrelation time of roughly 0.6 s. Port at the same rate: 0.265 at 0.05 s and -0.060 at 0.25 s, i.e. it decorrelates inside a single 20 fps frame. Re-measured at --fps 400 (dt = 0.0025 s): orig 1.000/1.000/0.999/0.977 at 0.003/0.005/0.01/0.05 s; port 0.950/0.877/0.739/0.170 at the same lags, giving a port half-decorrelation time of ~0.021 s. The port's field evolves about 30x too fast.
The ~40x spatial and ~30x temporal errors are the same order of magnitude, which points at ONE shared scale constant on the noise/field input rather than three separate bugs.

Spatial envelope: the original has a strong centre-weighted radial envelope, the port has none. 60 s time-averaged per-column luminance on the 16x16 grid — orig: 17 20 27 33 38 56 73 86 85 72 59 52 40 32 28 25 (peak ~86 at columns 7-8, ~5x the ~17-25 at the edges); per-row: 16 20 24 39 53 64 74 85 87 74 56 37 29 29 31 24. Port per-column: 20 16 23 22 17 20 19 14 15 16 18 15 10 25 17 13 (flat within noise); per-row: 18 19 17 17 25 20 17 20 17 19 12 14 18 16 16 15. The port's brightness is uniform across the rig where the original's concentrates in the middle.

Brightness and coverage. At 160x160, t=0: the original lights 16502/25600 pixels above value 40 (64% coverage) with value p50 192, p90 255, p99 255 and saturation p10 0.28 (the desaturated near-white cores). The port lights 4418/25600 (17% coverage) with value p50 107, p90 254 and saturation p10 0.50 — its peaks do reach full value, but it never produces the original's broad white/pale cores, and whole-rig mean brightness is 46-49 (orig) vs 19-21 (port) on every window and rig tried.

Colour. Brightness-weighted hue histogram at 160x160 t=0 (15-degree bins, percent of luminance): orig 105:11 120:15 135:13 150:13 165:13 180:14 195:13 210:6 plus 2% at 0 — a green-through-cyan band centred near 150 degrees. Port: 135:3 150:8 165:9 180:10 195:12 210:15 225:16 240:17 255:10 — a cyan-through-violet band centred near 225 degrees. The port's palette is shifted roughly +70 degrees toward blue/violet and is missing the original's green end almost entirely.

Both sides are time-based, not frame-coupled. Mean brightness is 46 (orig) and 19 (port) at --fps 10, 20 and 40 alike. The orig motion stat scales as ~1/fps (5 / 2.6 / 1 at 10/20/40 fps), the expected signature of a fixed per-second evolution rate sampled at different intervals. The port's motion triple (27 / 23 / 18) is saturated rather than informative because it decorrelates within one frame at all three rates; the --fps 400 decorrelation curve above confirms its rate is fixed in seconds, so there is no frame-rate-coupling bug on either side.

Seed independence: --seed 1234 reproduces the seed-1 stats exactly on both sides (orig mean 46 motion 3, port mean 19 motion 23), so neither side is RNG-driven and the divergence is fully deterministic.

Steady state is fine on both sides — neither dies, freezes or saturates. --skip 60 (12 s @ 20 fps): orig mean 61 motion 6, port mean 21 motion 25. --skip 120: orig mean 65 motion 5, port mean 21 motion 25. The 240 s @ 2 fps survey shows the original holding its centre-weighted envelope and continuous morph for the whole window with no regime boundaries, and the port holding uniform speckle for the whole window. The baseline's port 'rising' / orig 'decaying' brightnessTrend flags are just the 6 s window sitting on one slow swing of each side, not drift.

The same divergence reproduces on a non-default rig: --rig strip --pixels 120, 12 s @ 20 fps. The orig waterfall is a set of broad, smooth, slowly-drifting vertical filaments several pixels wide, coherent over the whole window (mean 55, motion 3). The port waterfall shows the same vertical-filament family at roughly a tenth the width, much dimmer and sparser (mean 20, motion 19).
feedback: Primary fix, worth far more than everything else combined: the port's field is evaluated at roughly 40x too high a SPATIAL frequency and roughly 30x too fast in TIME. Measured on a 160x160 grid, the original's luminance stays above 0.6 correlation out to an 80-pixel lag (half the canvas) while the port drops below 0.5 correlation at a 2.0-pixel lag; measured at --fps 400, the original's half-decorrelation time is ~0.6 s while the port's is ~0.021 s. Because the two error factors are the same order of magnitude, look first for a single shared multiplier applied to the field/noise inputs (or a coordinate normalisation that was dropped so pixel indices, not 0..1 coordinates, are being fed in). Target: on a 16x16 grid the original's field should be smooth enough that adjacent pixels correlate at ~0.85; the port currently correlates at ~0.05.

Second: the original's field has a strong centre-weighted radial envelope that the port lacks entirely. Time-averaged over 60 s on the 16x16 grid the original's per-column brightness runs 17 -> 86 -> 25 from left edge to centre to right edge (and 16 -> 87 -> 24 top to bottom), a ~5x centre-to-edge ratio; the port's is flat at 10-25 across every column and row. Whatever radial/distance-from-centre falloff term the original applies is missing or has no effect in the port.

Third, palette: the original's brightness-weighted hue sits in a green-to-cyan band centred near 150 degrees (105-210 degrees, peaking at 120-135), while the port sits in a cyan-to-violet band centred near 225 degrees (135-270, peaking at 225-240). The port needs its hue mapping rotated back roughly -70 degrees so the green end is restored; it currently produces no green at all.

Fourth, brightness/coverage, which may partly fall out of the scale fix: at 160x160 the original lights 64% of pixels above value 40 with a median lit value of 192 and desaturated near-white cores (saturation 10th percentile 0.28); the port lights 17% with median 107 and never desaturates below 0.50. Whole-rig mean brightness is 46-49 orig vs 19-21 port on every window and rig tested. After fixing the scale, re-check whether the port still lacks the pale/white cores and whether an extra gain or a lower saturation floor is needed.

Nothing else needs work: both sides have zero controls (matching), neither binds sensors, both are deterministic and seed-independent, both are time-based rather than frame-coupled, and the port's steady state over 132 s is stable — it does not decay, freeze or saturate. The port is one scale constant plus an envelope term plus a hue rotation away from being a plausible match; a re-verify after those three changes is worthwhile.

For the re-verify: the decisive cheap tests are (a) neighbour-correlation vs lag on a --grid 160x160 dump, which must reach orig's 0.98/0.92/0.81 at lags 1/8/16 px rather than the port's 0.74/0.17/0.06; (b) whole-frame temporal correlation at --fps 400, which must be ~0.98 at dt=0.05 s rather than 0.17; (c) the 60 s time-averaged per-column profile on the default 16x16 grid, which must show the ~5x centre peak.
